text:
samir.support: FYI customer reported streaming answers cutting off after a reconnect. They say final JSON never arrives and finish_reason is missing. Repro steps and curl pasted below. They hit this with our hosted API; claiming it’s intermittent but reproducible with repeated reconnects.

janet.eng: rough TL;DR of the repro?

samir.support: customer steps (short):
1) start SSE stream to /v1/streams with `model=redwood-x-small`
2) intentionally drop connection client-side, then reconnect using resume headers we give
3) response resumes but last chunk is truncated — final closing brace missing, no finish_reason. Happens ~1/20 runs.

samir.support: they included this curl to reproduce:
```
# open stream
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-x-small","prompt":"long reply...","resume_id":"abc123"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams
# then kill the client mid-stream and re-run with same resume_id
```

devon-rt: can they paste raw bytes of the truncated tail? sometimes nginx/tcp proxies chop trailing bytes.

samir.support: they pasted a snippet (raw chunk as received):
```
data: {"token":"...","text":"...","finish_reason":
```

(note the finish_reason field key is present but value and trailing }} are missing)

nick-infra: interesting. any 5xx or 499 in our logs around their request ids? samir can you share request-id?

samir.support: request-id: rwd-2026-03-02-7f3c, logs attached. customer said they saw a 200 at reconnect but the stream ended abruptly.

nick-infra: pulling logs — I see the initial stream session, then a resume call at +2s. Upstream show `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header` in one instance and an odd `write: broken pipe` from the worker in another. Might be worker hitting write timeout when client reconnects.

janet.eng: could be our resume path that stitches KV cache/mid-state. If resume tries to flush a buffered chunk with `Content-Length` vs chunked-encoding mismatch it'll send partial frame. Do we have any code that switches transfer-encoding mid-stream on resume?

devon-rt: also check the client-side reconnect sequence. If client sends a `Range`-like resume or a `last_event_id` and we re-emit partially, the SSE event framing can end up split across packets. Some clients will parse until socket close; if close happens early they lose the tail brace.

samir.support: customer says they use node-fetch in browser and do manual reconnect logic. They said switching to a simple `EventSource` made it slightly more stable but still reproducible.

nick-infra: I added additional logging on the resume path and increased the write timeout for the streaming worker on the canary cluster. Re-ran the customer's exact repro 50 times locally with a proxy that simulates mid-flight disconnects. Initially saw ~3 failures. After the timeout bump, failures dropped to 0/50.

janet.eng: that suggests we were closing the socket too early during resume flush. Quick patch idea: ensure resume handler drains buffered output fully before honoring client reattach ack. Also add explicit `finish_reason` marshaling that guarantees the final event is written atomically (single write syscall) if possible.

devon-rt: can we also make the streaming client library retry/resume idempotently by detecting truncated JSON? e.g., if last SSE event payload is invalid JSON, client should request a hard restart or ask server for `replay_from` offset. But we need server fix first.

samir.support: customer asked if this could be billing-related or auth. They saw successful auth each time (200) when reconnecting; no auth failures. Billing unaffected.

nick-infra: creating internal ticket INFRA-4812 and rolling the write-timeout change to canary. Patch details: increase write timeout from 5s -> 15s for streaming workers and make the resume flush use a synchronous write path.

ops-bot: INFRA-4812 created by nick-infra. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-4812

samir.support: customer willing to test workaround. I sent them a canary URL and asked to reproduce.

janet.eng: opened PR to ensure `finish_reason` always emitted even if the socket closes mid-flush — server will buffer final event until ack from kernel write. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/2978 (small change in resume handler).

devon-rt: long-term we should add a checksum or event sequence number in SSE meta so clients can detect missing tail token and auto-retry. Filing follow-up: RT-1220.

samir.support: update from customer after canary test: they ran 100 reconnect cycles, 0 failures. They reported fixed.

janet.eng: nice. action items:
- nick: roll write-timeout increase to prod and monitor 24h. (INFRA-4812)
- janet: merge PR and add unit test simulating mid-socket-close. (PR 2978)
- devon: client-side guidance doc — how to detect truncated SSE JSON and recommended retry/backoff. (RT-1220)

nick-infra: rolling prod change now (starting canary -> prod). I'll watch for 5xx/500/499 regressions.

samir.support: closing loop with customer now and sending summary + workaround in case they see recurrence.

janet.eng: note for postmortem: root cause was aggressive write timeout + non-atomic final event emission during resume. Mitigations: longer timeout, atomic final write, client-side detection.

samir.support: resolved for customer. Marking thread resolved. :white_check_mark:
